claims.text: The premelting and melting behavior of Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by the interplay of atomic size mismatch and local chemical ordering.
Atomic size mismatch and local chemical ordering create nanoscale regions with different cohesive energies.
Nanoscale variations in cohesive energy influence the onset and progression of melting.
The nanoparticles are initially solid Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The proposed intervention is gradual heating across the premelting and melting range.
Vacuum or inert-gas conditions prevent oxidation during heating.
Chemical complexity and atomic size mismatch produce local variations in cohesive energy in these nanoparticles.
Regions with lower cohesive energy begin premelting first.
Regions with higher cohesive energy resist melting until higher temperatures.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles will begin premelting at a lower temperature than similarly sized single-metal nanoparticles.
Their melting transition will span a broader temperature range because cohesive energy is heterogeneously distributed.
Similarly sized pure nickel or pure cobalt nanoparticles are expected to exhibit sharper melting transitions.
Similarly sized pure nickel or pure cobalt nanoparticles are expected to have higher premelting onset temperatures.
The hypothesis is limited to compositionally similar high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles in the 5–50 nm size range under controlled heating.
The hypothesis may not apply to bulk high-entropy alloys or nanoparticles with substantially different size distributions.
The relative contributions of atomic size mismatch and local chemical ordering may vary with composition and particle size.
DSC and in situ TEM measurements on high-entropy-alloy and size-matched single-metal nanoparticles provide the proposed controlled comparison.
A sharper melting transition or higher premelting onset temperature in the high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles than in the single-metal controls would falsify the stated prediction.
